Thanks Marissa — attaching our quick annotations (edgeworks_vpc_segment_v2_annotated.pdf). A few notes up front:

- NAT behavior: by default our onsite NVAs perform SNAT for tenant egress to the internet (source replaced with site egress IP). We can preserve source for Redwood control-plane traffic if you require persistent source IPs, but that requires passing through a non-NATed path to the control-plane collector.

- Telemetry egress: our preference is regional aggregator (us-west-2) for metrics/logs. We can firewall a direct collector endpoint if Redwood provides a static destination IP/CIDR and mTLS certificate thumbprint.

- BGP / peering: we can accept private ASNs; prefer to avoid 64512-64519 (reserved in our edge fabric). We propose using 64550/64551 pair for primary/backup. Please confirm your expected ASN and the announced prefixes for the tenant overlay.

Questions for Redwood:
1) Do you require control-plane connections originate from a stable IP per tenant (we can map to a transit IP but will add an ACL step)?
2) Are there minimum port ranges the control-plane needs opened (beyond 443/8443 for API/telemetry)?

We added inline comments in the PDF and a lightweight drawio share: https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1a2b3c-edgeworks-vpc-refs (diagram: controlplane_sequence.drawio.svg).

I can join a sync tomorrow at 11:00-11:30 PT or 15:00-15:30 PT — either works.

Regards,

On Fri, Aug 7, 2027 at 13:40, Anoop Patel <ap@edgeworks.io> wrote:
> We can preserve source for Redwood control-plane traffic if you require persistent source IPs...

Thanks Anoop — a few technical clarifications from our side that should help the runbook and acceptance checklist:

- Control-plane egress expectations: Redwood control-plane nodes (hosted) prefer incoming connections from fixed CIDRs per-customer for short-lived RPC over TLS. If EdgeWorks can present a stable transit IP / NAT pool for that purpose it simplifies auth and rate-limiting on our side.

- Ports: Primary is 443 for API/control; 8443 used by the internal agent for health/metrics in some older stacks. We'll treat 8443 as optional but please allow it during smoke.

- mTLS: strong preference for mutual TLS for telemetry ingestion. If that's not possible, we accept TLS + token over 443 but will flag it in the compliance tracker (less preferred).

- BGP: Jonas notes: avoid 169.254/16 and RFC1918 collisions, provide the exact announced prefixes in advance. We recommend announcing only the transit /28 to Redwood for control-plane acceptance; tenant overlay pools (10.x/16 ranges) are fine behind SNAT.

Proposed acceptance checklist (short):
1) Demarc acceptance test: ping from Redwood probe to provided transit IP (ICMP/443 TCP) — pass
2) Control-plane TLS handshake to collector endpoint using Redwood test cert — pass
3) BGP session established and routes visible to Redwood (transit /28 present) — pass
4) Telemetry path validation: sample metric shows up in region aggregator within 90s — pass

I added the checklist to our shared Confluence page: https://redwood.atlassian.net/l/cp/EDGE-211 — please confirm and we can finalize for the runbook.

If EdgeWorks prefers, we can do the 11:00 PT slot (Marissa: can you confirm?).
